set_title: Osteo- names: porosis vs petrosis vs malacia vs myelitis vs arthritis vs sarcoma
stem: A 70-year-old woman has sudden mid-back pain after lifting a grocery bag. She went through menopause at 50 and has never taken hormone therapy. Calcium, phosphate and alkaline phosphatase are normal. A spine x-ray shows a wedge compression fracture of T12 and thin, pale vertebrae.
oneliner: 70F, postmenopausal + back pain after lifting + vertebral compression fracture, normal Ca, phosphate and ALP → ?

whyNot.A: Osteomalacia has high alkaline phosphatase and low phosphate; hers are **normal**
whyNot.B: Osteopetrosis gives dense bone and cytopenias; her vertebrae are **thin and pale**
whyNot.D: Osteoarthritis wears joints, not vertebral bodies; she has a **compression fracture**
whyNot.E: Osteosarcoma is a mass; she is **70 with a minor-trauma fracture**

why: Porous bone: low bone mass with normal mineralization. **A postmenopausal woman with a vertebral fracture and normal labs** is osteoporosis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Low bone mass, normal labs; vertebral fractures**
**Low vitamin D; low Ca, phosphate; high ALP**
**Bone infection; S. aureus; Salmonella in sickle cell**

idea.rule: Fragility fracture + normal Ca, phosphate and ALP = osteoporosis.
also: Estrogen loss raises osteoclast activity
Bisphosphonates block osteoclasts

set_title: Osteo- names: porosis vs petrosis vs malacia vs myelitis vs arthritis vs sarcoma
stem: A 4-year-old boy has had two long-bone fractures after minor falls. He is pale, has an enlarged liver and spleen, and has had recent facial weakness and hearing loss. Hemoglobin and platelet counts are low. X-rays show uniformly dense bones with an Erlenmeyer flask shape of the distal femurs.
oneliner: 4M, fractures after minor falls + anemia, low platelets, big spleen, cranial nerve palsies + very dense bones → ?

whyNot.A: Osteomalacia gives soft, bowed bones; his bones are **dense on x-ray**
whyNot.C: Osteoarthritis wears joints in adults; he has **dense bones and marrow failure**
whyNot.D: Osteosarcoma is one painful mass; his **whole skeleton is dense with cytopenias**
whyNot.E: Osteoporosis makes thin bones in older adults; his are **dense with low blood counts**

why: Stone bone: osteoclasts cannot resorb bone, so it is dense but brittle. **Fractures, cytopenias and cranial nerve palsies with dense bones** is osteopetrosis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Low bone mass, normal labs; vertebral fractures**
**Low vitamin D; low Ca, phosphate; high ALP**
**Bone infection; S. aureus; Salmonella in sickle cell**

idea.rule: Dense yet brittle bone + marrow failure + cranial nerve palsies = osteopetrosis.
also: Carbonic anhydrase II or osteoclast acid defect
Bone marrow transplant is curative

set_title: Osteo- names: porosis vs petrosis vs malacia vs myelitis vs arthritis vs sarcoma
stem: A 40-year-old woman who wears full-body covering and avoids sunlight has had diffuse bone pain and proximal weakness for 6 months. She waddles when she walks. Calcium and phosphate are low, alkaline phosphatase is high, and 25-hydroxyvitamin D is low. X-rays show thin lucent lines across the femoral necks.
oneliner: 40F, no sun exposure + bone pain, waddling gait + low Ca and phosphate, high ALP, lucent lines → ?

whyNot.A: Osteoporosis has normal calcium, phosphate; hers show **low Ca, low phosphate, high ALP**
whyNot.B: Osteosarcoma is a focal mass; she has **diffuse pain and low vitamin D**
whyNot.C: Osteopetrosis makes dense bone; she has **low vitamin D and lucent lines**
whyNot.D: Osteomyelitis is a febrile infection; she has **diffuse pain, no fever, low vitamin D**

why: Soft bone: osteoid is made but not mineralized. **Low vitamin D with low calcium and phosphate and high ALP** is osteomalacia (rickets in children).

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Low bone mass, normal labs; vertebral fractures**
**Low vitamin D; low Ca, phosphate; high ALP**
**Bone infection; S. aureus; Salmonella in sickle cell**

idea.rule: Vitamin D deficiency in adults, high ALP = osteomalacia; in children, rickets.
also: Looser zones: lucent pseudofractures
Treat with vitamin D and calcium

set_title: Osteo- names: porosis vs petrosis vs malacia vs myelitis vs arthritis vs sarcoma
stem: A 15-year-old boy has had pain and swelling above his right knee for 2 months, worse at night. The distal femur is tender and warm over a firm mass. A knee x-ray shows a destructive lesion with new bone fanning outward in a sunburst pattern and a raised edge of periosteum.
oneliner: 15M + 2 months of night pain and a firm mass above the knee + sunburst pattern, raised periosteum on x-ray → ?

whyNot.A: Osteomyelitis has fever; he has a **firm mass, sunburst pattern**
whyNot.B: Osteoarthritis occurs in older adults; he is **15 with a bone-forming mass**
whyNot.D: Osteoporosis thins bone without a mass; he has a **destructive sunburst lesion**
whyNot.E: Osteomalacia is diffuse softening; his is a **focal mass with periosteal elevation**

why: Bone-forming cancer: malignant cells make osteoid. **A teenager's knee mass with sunburst pattern and Codman triangle** is osteosarcoma.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Low bone mass, normal labs; vertebral fractures**
**Low vitamin D; low Ca, phosphate; high ALP**
**Bone infection; S. aureus; Salmonella in sickle cell**

idea.rule: Teen distal femur mass + sunburst or Codman triangle = osteosarcoma.
also: Retinoblastoma (RB) and p53 mutations raise risk
Lungs are the usual metastasis site

set_title: Thyroiditis names: Hashimoto, de Quervain (and the de Quervain of the wrist), postpartum, Graves
stem: A 30-year-old woman has had pain on the thumb side of her right wrist for 3 weeks, since she began carrying her newborn. Pain worsens when she lifts him. There is tenderness and swelling over the radial styloid. When she folds her thumb into her fist and her wrist is bent toward the little finger, the pain is sharp. Her thyroid is normal.
oneliner: 30F, new mother + radial wrist pain when lifting + tender radial styloid + positive Finkelstein test → ?

whyNot.B: Thumb-base arthritis gives grind pain in older adults; she has **positive Finkelstein**
whyNot.C: Subacute thyroiditis is neck pain; hers is at the **radial styloid, thyroid normal**
whyNot.D: Hashimoto is a painless goiter; she has **a positive Finkelstein test**
whyNot.E: Postpartum thyroiditis affects the thyroid; her gland is **normal with wrist pain**

why: Same surname, different organ: inflamed sheath of two thumb tendons. **Radial wrist pain with a positive Finkelstein test** is de Quervain tenosynovitis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: same name: thumb tendon sheath inflammation

idea.rule: Radial wrist pain + positive Finkelstein = de Quervain tenosynovitis.
also: Abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis
Thumb spica splint; steroid injection

set_title: -uria words: what is in the urine (blood, hemoglobin, myoglobin, odd metabolites)
stem: A 20-year-old man collapses at the end of a marathon on a hot day. He has severe muscle pain and passes dark brown urine. Creatine kinase is 85,000 U/L and potassium is 6.0 mEq/L. Haptoglobin is normal. Urine dipstick is positive for blood, but microscopy shows no red cells.
oneliner: 20M, marathon in heat + muscle pain, dark urine + CK 85,000 + dipstick blood, no red cells, normal haptoglobin → ?

whyNot.A: Alkaptonuria darkens urine on standing from birth; he has **muscle injury and CK 85,000**
whyNot.C: Hematuria shows red cells; his sample has **none on microscopy**
whyNot.D: Hemoglobinuria has low haptoglobin from hemolysis; his is **normal with high CK**
whyNot.E: Phenylketonuria gives a musty odor in infants; he has **dark urine and rhabdomyolysis**

why: Muscle pigment in urine after muscle breakdown. **Dark urine, positive dipstick blood without red cells and CK in the tens of thousands** is myoglobinuria.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Dipstick blood, no red cells; CK very high**

idea.rule: Dipstick blood, no red cells, high CK, normal haptoglobin = myoglobinuria.
also: Rhabdomyolysis can cause acute tubular necrosis
Treat with saline; watch potassium

set_title: Paget names: bone remodeling vs breast and skin cancer (and an effort clot)
stem: A 68-year-old man says his hat no longer fits and he has new hearing loss. Alkaline phosphatase is 900 U/L, with normal calcium and phosphate. Skull x-ray shows thickened bone with mixed lytic and sclerotic areas.
oneliner: 68-year-old man, larger hat size + hearing loss + ALP 900, normal calcium + thick mixed skull lesions → ?

whyNot.B: Paget disease of the breast is nipple cancer; he has **skull thickening, high ALP**
whyNot.C: Extramammary Paget disease is a skin plaque; he has **bone thickening and high ALP**
whyNot.D: Paget-Schroetter is an arm vein clot; he has **skull thickening and hearing loss**
whyNot.E: Page kidney causes hypertension from renal compression; he has **skull thickening and high ALP**

why: Osteoclast-driven, disordered remodeling producing thick, weak bone. **Larger hat size, hearing loss and isolated high ALP with normal calcium**; treat with bisphosphonates.

idea.rule: Same surname, four diseases: bone, breast, vulva, vein. Match the organ.
also: Risk of osteosarcoma, high-output failure
Mosaic bone on histology

set_title: Paget names: bone remodeling vs breast and skin cancer (and an effort clot)
stem: A 22-year-old male baseball pitcher has sudden swelling, heaviness and blue discoloration of the right arm after a game. Duplex ultrasound shows a clot in the right subclavian vein. Arterial pulses are normal.
oneliner: 22-year-old baseball pitcher, sudden swollen blue right arm after play + subclavian vein clot + normal pulses → ?

whyNot.A: Paget disease of bone is skeletal; he has an **arm vein clot**
whyNot.C: Paget disease of the breast is nipple cancer; he has an **arm vein clot**
whyNot.D: Extramammary Paget disease is a vulvar plaque; he has a **subclavian vein clot**
whyNot.E: Page kidney is renal compression causing hypertension; he has a **swollen blue arm**

why: Effort thrombosis of the subclavian vein from repetitive overhead arm use (venous thoracic outlet). **Sudden swollen blue arm after overhead activity** with a subclavian clot.

idea.rule: Paget-Schroetter: a vein clot in a young athlete's arm.
also: Venous thoracic outlet syndrome
Treat with thrombolysis, rib resection

set_title: R- eponyms: Reye, Rett, Reiter, Riedel, Richter, Raynaud
stem: A 24-year-old man has had pain and swelling of the right knee and heels for 1 week. He has red, irritated eyes and burning on urination. Three weeks ago he had a Chlamydia urethritis. Tests show he carries HLA-B27, and joint fluid culture is sterile.
oneliner: 24M, knee and heel arthritis + red eyes + dysuria, 3 weeks after urethritis, HLA-B27 → ?

whyNot.A: Raynaud is finger vasospasm; he has **sterile arthritis with eye, urethral signs**
whyNot.B: Rett syndrome is a childhood regression in girls; he is **24 with arthritis**
whyNot.C: Richter transformation needs CLL; he has **no leukemia**
whyNot.D: Riedel thyroiditis is a fibrotic goiter; he has **joint, eye and urethral disease**

why: Arthritis reacting to a distant infection. **Conjunctivitis, urethritis and arthritis after Chlamydia, HLA-B27** fit it.

idea.rule: Reactive arthritis = can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree.
also: Sterile joint fluid after Chlamydia or enteric infection
Eponym Reiter is now discouraged

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **CLL with sudden node growth, high LDH**
**Fingers white, blue, then red in cold**

set_title: Spondylo- names: wear, break, slip, inflammation or infection of the vertebrae
stem: A 15-year-old girl who trains in gymnastics 20 hours a week has had low back pain for 2 months. The pain worsens when she arches her back and eases with rest. She has no fever, and strength, reflexes and sensation in her legs are normal. No step-off is felt along the spine. An oblique x-ray of the lumbar spine shows a lucent line across the pars interarticularis of L5, and a lateral view shows normal alignment.
oneliner: 15F gymnast + low back pain worse on arching + lucent line across the L5 pars, normal alignment → ?

whyNot.A: Spondylosis is age-related wear in older adults; she is **15 with a pars lucency**
whyNot.C: Ankylosing spondylitis pain improves with exercise; hers is **worse arching, better with rest**
whyNot.D: Spondylolisthesis means a forward slip; she has **normal alignment and no step-off**
whyNot.E: Spondylodiscitis is a febrile disc infection; she has **no fever and a pars lucency**

why: Vertebra + break: a pars stress fracture with no slip. **A gymnast with pain on extension, pars lucency and normal alignment** has spondylolysis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Narrowed discs and osteophytes in older adult**
**Pars fracture, no slip; Scottie dog collar**
**Young man, stiffness better with exercise; sacroiliitis**
**Fever; disc and both endplates on MRI**

idea.rule: Lysis = pars broken, vertebra in place; once it slides, it is listhesis.
also: Repeated hyperextension, most often at L5
Oblique x-ray: collar on the Scottie dog

set_title: Spondylo- names: wear, break, slip, inflammation or infection of the vertebrae
stem: A 16-year-old boy who plays as a lineman in football has had low back pain and tight hamstrings for 6 months. Bending forward is limited, and a step-off is felt over the lower lumbar spinous processes. He has no fever or morning stiffness. A lateral x-ray shows the L5 vertebral body displaced forward on S1 by about one quarter of its width.
oneliner: 16M lineman + back pain, tight hamstrings, palpable step-off + L5 shifted forward on S1 → ?

whyNot.A: Spondylodiscitis is a febrile spine infection; he has **no fever and L5 shifted forward**
whyNot.B: Ankylosing spondylitis brings long morning stiffness; he has **no stiffness and a step-off**
whyNot.C: Spondylolysis is a pars fracture with normal alignment; his **L5 is displaced forward**
whyNot.E: Spondylosis is degenerative wear in older adults; he is **16 with a slipped vertebra**

why: Vertebra + slipping: one vertebra slides forward on the one below. **A palpable step-off with L5 forward on S1** is spondylolisthesis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Narrowed discs and osteophytes in older adult**
**Pars fracture, no slip; Scottie dog collar**
**Young man, stiffness better with exercise; sacroiliitis**
**Fever; disc and both endplates on MRI**

idea.rule: Lysis = broken; listhesis = slipped. A step-off means listhesis.
also: Teens: bilateral pars fractures; older adults: L4-L5 wear
Graded I to V (Meyerding) by slip

set_title: Spondylo- names: wear, break, slip, inflammation or infection of the vertebrae
stem: A 24-year-old man has had low back and buttock pain for 8 months, with morning stiffness that lasts over an hour. The pain wakes him in the second half of the night, improves with exercise, and worsens with rest. Forward bending of the lumbar spine and chest expansion are reduced. Last year he had a painful red eye with sensitivity to light. Pelvic x-rays show erosions and sclerosis of both sacroiliac joints.
oneliner: 24M + 8 months of back pain with long morning stiffness, better with exercise + reduced chest expansion + red eye + bilateral sacroiliitis → ?

whyNot.A: Spondylosis is wear in older adults; he is **24 with stiffness easing on exercise**
whyNot.B: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy causes clumsy hands; he has **low back pain and sacroiliitis**
whyNot.C: Spondylodiscitis is a febrile infection at one level; he has **bilateral sacroiliitis and uveitis**
whyNot.D: Spondylolysis hurts on extension; his pain **eases with exercise, worsens with rest**

why: Fusing stiffness + vertebra + inflammation. **A young man with morning stiffness easing on exercise, past uveitis and bilateral sacroiliitis** has ankylosing spondylitis (HLA-B27).

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Narrowed discs and osteophytes in older adult**
**Pars fracture, no slip; Scottie dog collar**
**Young man, stiffness better with exercise; sacroiliitis**
**Fever; disc and both endplates on MRI**

idea.rule: Young adult back pain better with exercise, worse with rest = ankylosing spondylitis.
also: HLA-B27; uveitis, aortic regurgitation, apical fibrosis
NSAIDs first, then TNF-alpha or IL-17 inhibitors

set_title: Spondylo- names: wear, break, slip, inflammation or infection of the vertebrae
stem: A 68-year-old woman has had neck pain and stiffness for several years that worsens toward the end of the day and with prolonged reading. She has no fever, weight loss, hand clumsiness or trouble walking. Strength, reflexes, sensation and gait are normal. A cervical spine x-ray shows narrowed disc spaces at C5-C6 and C6-C7 with osteophytes at the vertebral margins, and alignment is normal.
oneliner: 68F + years of neck pain worse by evening + normal neuro exam + narrowed discs with osteophytes → ?

whyNot.B: Spondylolisthesis means a forward slip; her x-ray shows **normal alignment**
whyNot.C: Ankylosing spondylitis starts young, eases with activity; she is **68, worse with use**
whyNot.D: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy adds cord signs; she has **normal reflexes, hands and gait**
whyNot.E: Spondylolysis is a pars fracture in young athletes; she is **68 with osteophytes**

why: Vertebra + condition (wear): osteoarthritis of the spine. **Years of mechanical neck pain, narrowed discs, osteophytes and a normal neuro exam** is spondylosis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Narrowed discs and osteophytes in older adult**
**Pars fracture, no slip; Scottie dog collar**
**Young man, stiffness better with exercise; sacroiliitis**
**Fever; disc and both endplates on MRI**

also: Most at C5-C6, C6-C7 and L4-S1
Upper motor neuron signs mean cord compression
